messages:
rachel: Quick sync — sketching a new UX idea: 'fallback exposure budget' for rollouts. want quick reactions before i mock it up.

sam: tl;dr — what's the problem this solves vs percent-based canaries?

rachel: Percent is too coarse. We need to limit absolute exposure (and cost/quality surface) not just rate. idea: budget is tokens/requests per window + burn-rate cap. UX shows both tokens left + estimated regression risk.

lex: interesting. So instead of "route 5% -> fallback" it's more like "allow up to 10k fallback tokens/day"?

rachel: Exactly. Example: fallback_budget: tokens_per_hour=2000 scope=route. If burst exceeds window we pause fallback and notify. Keeps customers' users from seeing long tail bad outputs while we ramp.

maya: I like auditability angle. We should show: budget remaining, historical burn rate chart, last N sampled outputs from fallback, and a one-click pause. Also add signal thresholds (latency/error-rate) to auto-throttle the budget. :chart_with_downwards_trend:

sam: How does this interact with quotas/billing? If fallback uses a larger model, cost could spike even with tiny request counts. Need visible cost projection in the UI.

rachel: Agreed — plan is to show estimated cost burn as part of the rollout summary and a warning if projected spend > threshold. Default policy ties budget to model variant id + rollout id so accounting is straightforward.

lex: Edge case: multi-route rollouts that share the same model variant. Do we expose per-route budgets or a shared pool?

rachel: Default per-route, but admins can opt-in to a shared pool for global experiments. UI will surface spillover behavior: "if route A exceeds budget, optionally borrow from pool B?" — defaults to false.

sam: Operationally we need audit logs for changes. Who bumped budget, old/new values, reason. Must be immutable and tied to rollout version.

maya: Telemetry needs: budget_consumed_total, budget_remaining, budget_pause_events, sampled_fallback_examples; alerts for unusual burn-rate delta (>x% / 10m). Also a small API to fetch current budget state for dashboards.

rachel: proto config snippet i tossed in the thread:

```
fallback_budget:
  type: "tokens_per_hour"
  limit: 5000
  scope: "route"
  auto_throttle:
    enabled: true
    latency_threshold_ms: 600
    error_rate_threshold: 0.02
```

lex: UX nit — slider alone is ambiguous. show both slider and numeric field: percentage, token count, and estimated daily cost. Add tooltips: "what counts as a token".

sam: Ops: what happens if budget pauses in prod mid-rollout? Should we auto-fallback-back to primary or keep serving primary? Need safe default: pause fallback and roll back to primary variant.

rachel: agreed. default: pause fallback routing and create an incident breadcrumb. Admin can configure graceful handback vs instant revert.

devops-bot: deploy queued -> rollout-service / feature/fallback-budget-proto @1759876600

maya: next steps: rachel to produce 2 mock screens (route-level, shared-pool) + metrics contract. I'll draft alert rules and event names. sam will check billing hooks. lex will mock the slider + numeric combo.

rachel: perfect — i'll push a minimal prototype to the sandbox and link it in this thread when ready. anyone opposed to the concept?

lex: +1

sam: +1 from me, big 👍 for cost visibility

maya: +1, please include sampled outputs retention policy (privacy reqs).

rachel: thanks — i'll follow up with design files and an RFC link.
